exposure: Mode of misoprostol administration (vaginal vs. oral)
outcome: Interval from induction to 3 cm cervical dilatation
cohort: Obese women undergoing induction of labor with singleton, viable pregnancies beyond 37 weeks of gestation, with an initial Bishop score of 7 or less and cervical dilatation of less than 2 cm
finding: Vaginal misoprostol was associated with shorter time intervals from induction to 3 cm cervical dilatation and delivery compared to oral misoprostol in obese women undergoing induction of labor.
mod_finding: In a population of obese women undergoing induction of labor, vaginal administration of misoprostol was associated with shorter time intervals from the start of induction to the attainment of 3 cm of dilatation, as well as to delivery, without increasing the rate of cesarean deliveries.
